detailed_summary: This paper studies quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) with (r,δ)-locality, where any δ-1 erased qudits can be recovered by accessing only r other qudits. The authors focus on constructing optimal impure (r,δ)-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets, measured against the Singleton-like bound of Guruswami, Kshirsagar, and Trivedi (GKT-optimal). They first characterize the recovering sets and minimum locality of any CSS code using local relative distances, defined as relative minimum distances of punctured codes with respect to shortened codes. Then, they construct impure qLRCs as CSS codes from nested pairs of generalized monomial-Cartesian codes. By grouping monomials by their degree in the last variable, they reduce both minimum distances and local recovery to nested pairs of codes in the remaining variables, with coordinates sharing the same values of these variables forming disjoint recovering sets. This yields four infinite families of GKT-optimal impure (r,δ)-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets, and they determine their minimum localities and recovering sets for every admissible δ, except for a partial range in one family. Notably, the minimum localities need not be monotone in δ, and two families contain GKT-optimal impure subfamilies of CSS codes CSS(C,C) with (r,δ)-locality for some r < n-δ+1 at values of δ where C has no classical (r',δ)-locality for any 0 < r' < n.
key_contributions: Characterization of recovering sets and minimum locality of any CSS code via local relative distances, providing a general framework for analyzing locality in quantum codes.
Construction of four infinite families of GKT-optimal impure (r,δ)-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets using nested pairs of generalized monomial-Cartesian codes.
Determination of minimum localities and recovering sets for every admissible δ (except a partial range in one family), revealing that minimum locality need not be monotone in δ.
Identification of GKT-optimal impure subfamilies of CSS(C,C) with (r,δ)-locality for r < n-δ+1 at δ values where the classical code C has no (r',δ)-locality, demonstrating a purely quantum advantage.
methodology_analysis: The paper employs a code-theoretic approach, leveraging CSS quantum codes and classical algebraic geometry codes. The key methodological innovation is the use of local relative distances to characterize recovering sets and minimum locality for CSS codes. This reduces the problem of finding quantum locality to analyzing punctured and shortened classical codes. The construction uses generalized monomial-Cartesian codes, which are evaluation codes over Cartesian products. By grouping monomials by their degree in the last variable, the authors decompose the code into nested pairs of codes in fewer variables, enabling both distance and locality analysis. The disjoint recovering sets arise naturally from coordinates sharing the same values of the remaining variables. This algebraic structure allows explicit computation of parameters and proof of GKT-optimality.
results_analysis: The paper presents four infinite families of GKT-optimal impure (r,δ)-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets. For each family, the minimum locality r and the recovering sets are explicitly determined for all admissible δ, except for a partial range in one family. A notable finding is that the minimum locality is not necessarily monotone in δ, which contrasts with classical LRCs. Furthermore, two families yield GKT-optimal impure CSS codes CSS(C,C) with (r,δ)-locality for some r < n-δ+1 at δ values where the classical code C has no (r',δ)-locality for any 0 < r' < n. This demonstrates that quantum locality can exist even when the underlying classical code lacks locality, highlighting a quantum advantage. The results are significant as they provide explicit constructions meeting a Singleton-like bound and offer new insights into the structure of quantum LRCs.
strengths: Provides a general characterization of locality for CSS codes via local relative distances, which is a versatile tool for analyzing quantum LRCs.
Constructs explicit infinite families of GKT-optimal impure qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets, addressing a gap in the literature.
Reveals non-monotonicity of minimum locality in δ, an interesting phenomenon that challenges classical intuition.
Demonstrates a quantum advantage where CSS(C,C) codes exhibit locality even when the classical code does not, expanding the understanding of quantum LRCs.
limitations: The determination of minimum locality is incomplete for a partial range of δ in one family, leaving some parameters unresolved.
The constructions are limited to impure codes and specific algebraic families; it is unclear whether the techniques extend to other code families or pure codes.
The paper focuses on theoretical bounds and constructions; practical decoding algorithms and performance analysis are not addressed.
connections_to_research: This work is directly relevant to quantum physics, particularly quantum error correction and quantum information theory. Quantum LRCs are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum memories, where efficient recovery from erasures is crucial. The use of CSS codes and algebraic geometry connects to broader research in quantum coding theory. The characterization via local relative distances may inspire further studies on locality in quantum codes, and the quantum advantage demonstrated could motivate new directions in quantum code design.
overall_assessment: This paper makes a significant contribution to the theory of quantum locally recoverable codes by providing explicit constructions of GKT-optimal impure qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets. The novel characterization using local relative distances and the algebraic construction are technically sound and yield interesting results, including non-monotonic locality and a quantum advantage. The work is novel and of high quality, though some parameters remain unresolved and practical aspects are not explored. It is likely to be influential in the quantum coding community and stimulate further research on locality in quantum codes.
